title: Digital transformation and dynamic capabilities for sustainable sme advantage: Business model innovation mediation
summary: SMEs increasingly adopt digital technologies, yet adoption alone does not ensure sustainable competitive advantage. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, the resource-based view, and business model innovation literature, this study examines how digital transformation and dynamic capabilities relate to perceived sustainable competitive advantage through business model innovation. Using survey data from 400 SMEs in West Sumatra, Indonesia, the model was tested with PLS-SEM and robustness controls for firm age and size. The results show that digital transformation and dynamic capabilities positively relate to business model innovation and competitive advantage. Business model innovation is the strongest predictor, while dynamic capabilities have a larger total effect than digital transformation. Business model innovation partially mediates both relationships, and the results remain stable after controls. These findings show that SME competitiveness is capability-enabled and business-model-mediated, implying that support programs should extend beyond technology adoption toward capability development, business model renewal, and measurable competitive outcomes.

title: Full-Scope Supervision System, Accounting Information Quality, and the Corporate Information Environment
summary: Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2015 to 2024, this study exploits the staggered implementation of the Full-Scope Supervision System (FSS) and a multi-period difference-in-differences design to examine its effect on accounting information quality, measured by the absolute value of discretionary accruals (AbsDA). The results show that FSS significantly reduces AbsDA, indicating improved reporting quality and less earnings manipulation. The effect is stronger among firms with greater digital transformation, higher ownership concentration, lower analyst attention, and weaker information environments. Mechanism evidence points primarily to improvements in the information environment, while the role of analyst attention is more nuanced because it reflects both monitoring and information demand. These findings identify institutional supervision as an important external governance mechanism for improving corporate reporting quality.

title: Digital Transformation and Academic Library Serviceability in State-Owned Universities in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
summary: Digital transformation is redefining how academic libraries acquire, organise, preserve and deliver information. In Nigerian state-owned universities, however, the conversion of isolated technologies into dependable, user-centred services remains uneven. This study examined the influence of digital transformation on academic library serviceability in the three state-owned universities in Bayelsa State: Niger Delta University, University of Africa, Toru-Orua, and Bayelsa Medical University. Digital transformation was operationalised through three dimensions: digital infrastructure adequacy, librarians' digital competence, and digital service integration. A correlational survey design was adopted. Because the article is a methodological demonstration rather than a report of completed fieldwork, a clearly labelled simulated dataset of 240 valid library-user responses was generated to reflect plausible response patterns across the three institutions. The Digital Transformation and Library Serviceability Questionnaire contained 24 items measured on a four-point scale. Simulated reliability coefficients ranged from .82 to .88. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple and multiple regression were used, and all numerical analyses are reported in tables. Results indicated moderate digital infrastructure, relatively stronger staff digital competence, moderate digital service integration and moderate-tohigh library serviceability. Digital infrastructure significantly predicted serviceability (R² = .299, β = .547, p < .001); digital competence significantly predicted serviceability (R² = .361, β = .601, p < .001); and digital service integration was the strongest bivariate predictor (R² = .443, β = .666, p < .001). Jointly, the three dimensions explained 54.8% of the simulated variance in serviceability. The study concludes that technology acquisition alone is insufficient: infrastructure must be reliable, librarians must possess applied digital capabilities, and systems must be integrated into end-to-end user journeys. Recommendations include protected digital-library funding, continuous competency-based training, unified discovery and authentication, remote reference services, accessibility standards, service analytics and institutional digitaltransformation governance. The findings are illustrative and must not be represented as observations from real participants; they provide a defensible template for a future field study in Bayelsa State.

title: Unlocking the potential of data: the impact of data assets on corporate investment-financing maturity mismatches
summary: Purpose While existing studies document that data assets matter in business and managerial activities, the association between data assets and corporate investment-financing maturity mismatches remains unclear. We set out to explore their relationship and elucidate the mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Utilizing panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms, we use text analysis to measure the level of corporate data assets and empirically investigate the influence of data assets on investment-financing maturity mismatches. Findings We confirm a negative association between data assets and investment-financing maturity mismatches. When data assets increase by one standard deviation, investment-financing maturity mismatches improve by 5.02%. This improvement is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, those operating in highly market competition and technology-intensive enterprises. Mechanism analysis shows that data assets exert a resource effect to alleviate financing constraints, and exhibit a supervisory effect to attract media monitoring, thereby mitigating investment-financing maturity mismatches. Originality/value Our findings reveal mechanisms for effectively mitigating investment-financing maturity mismatches from the perspective of the increasingly prominent data assets. These new insights also advance the understanding of the theoretical and practical importance of data assets among investment-financing decision-making and management in emerging markets.

title: A STUDY ON FACTORS INFLUENCING INVESTORS’ BEHAVIOUR TOWARDS THE MONEY MARKET AND CAPITAL MARKET IN BANGALORE DISTRICT
summary: The financial market provides investors with diverse investment opportunities through money market and capital market instruments. Investors’ behaviour towards these markets is influenced by financial, economic, informational and behavioural factors. The present study, entitled “A Study on Factors Influencing Investors’ Behaviour towards Money Market and Capital Market”, aims to identify and assess the factors influencing investors’ behaviour towards money market and capital market investments in Bangalore District. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design and is based on primary and secondary data. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire from a sample of 410 investors, selected using the Yamane sampling method. Multiple regression analysis was employed to examine the influence of the selected factors on investors’ behaviour. The findings reveal that the money market regression model has an R² value of 0.713, indicating that 71.3% of the variation in investors’ behaviour is explained by the selected factors. Interest Rate/Rate of Return, Financial Literacy and Market Conditions emerged as major positive influences, while Risk and Safety, Inflation Rate, Tax Benefits and Investment Horizon showed significant negative relationships. Economic Stability and Availability of Information were found to be insignificant. In the capital market, the regression model recorded an R² value of 0.916, indicating that 91.6% of the variation in investor behaviour is explained by the selected factors. Expected Rate of Return, Liquidity and Income Level emerged as major positive influences, while Financial Literacy and Investor Sentiment and Behavioural Factors showed significant negative relationships. The study concludes that investors’ behaviour is multidimensional and differs according to the nature and characteristics of the financial market. The findings provide useful insights for investors, financial institutions, investment advisors and policymakers in developing appropriate investment strategies.

title: From IT-enabled organisational transformation to digital transformation: leadership strategies for value creation in manufacturing
summary: Digital Transformation (DT), which encompasses Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0, has been conceptualised and often paralleled with IT-Enabled Organizational Transformation (ITOT) by academia and practitioners. Despite their shared foundation in organisational transformation, the goals pursued are not the same, demanding different leadership profiles to either reinforce an organisation's existing value proposition and identity in ITOT or redefine its value proposition and establish a new organisational identity in DT. This paper aims to identify leadership strategies supporting value creation within organisations through the ITOT and DT journeys, including leadership competencies and practices related to the organisation's purpose with digital initiatives. This research employed a Fuzzy Delphi method based on a survey of 46 leaders involved in ITOT or DT in manufacturing companies in Brazil. Our findings reveal that leaders consider themselves mostly unprepared to navigate these organisational transformations in the manufacturing sector. The study highlights the need for leaders to create value beyond technological aspects and embrace a human-centric approach to change management that enables strategic organisational transformation. Our main contribution is a framework guiding the alignment between leadership strategies and competencies development to support ITOT and DT according to the organisation's purpose to become more sensing, smart, sustainable or social.

title: AI and Digital Transformation in the Renewable Energy Sector: A Strategic Framework for Sustainable Business Performance
summary: Purpose: The global shift towards clean energy necessitates robust business strategies to address challenges related to intermittent supply, operational inefficiencies, and evolving market conditions. This study fills a gap in strategic management literature by exploring the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Transformation (DT) in enhancing sustainable business performance within renewable energy enterprises. Design/Methodology/Approach: Utilizing the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study conducts a qualitative conceptual synthesis and systematic analysis of recent literature (2018–2026) to formulate an integrated strategic management framework. Findings: The study presents the AI-Driven Digital Transformation for Sustainable Energy (ADT-SE) framework. This model demonstrates that the alignment of technological drivers—such as predictive analytics, IoT, smart grids, and block chain—with core organizational capabilities significantly enhances financial performance, operational efficiency, and environmental stewardship. title: Biometric Authentication and Fraud Detection in Fintech Companies in Nigeria
summary: The increasing reliance on digital financial services in Nigeria has amplified concerns about fraud within the Fintech sector. This study investigates the role of biometric authentication technologies—specifically iris/retina scanning and fingerprint identification systems—in detecting and curbing fraud in Nigerian Fintech companies. Leveraging a descriptive survey research design, data were gathered from 170 respondents comprising customers and staff of selected Fintech firms through structured questionnaires. The study utilized descriptive and inferential statistics to analyze the relationship between biometric technologies and fraud detection. Findings reveal a significant positive relationship between iris/retina biometric systems and fraud detection, suggesting that advanced biometric technologies enhance the security infrastructure of Fintech services. However, despite these advancements, fraud persists, emphasizing the need for continuous innovation and multi-layered security frameworks. The study recommends enhanced adoption of biometric systems alongside other robust authentication measures to strengthen fraud prevention mechanisms in Nigeria’ s rapidly evolving digital financial landscape.

title: Bibliometric analysis of research trends in digital transformation and mental health from 2014 to 2024
summary: Abstract Digital transformation has significantly reshaped modern society, with important implications for mental health. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution, main contributors, and thematic development of research on digital transformation and its psychological effects. A bibliometric analysis was conducted on studies indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed databases, covering the period January 1, 2014 to June 20, 2024. A total of 2287 publications were initially identified, of which 1606 were included in the analysis. The study employed the Biblioshiny application within the Bibliometrix package in RStudio. The bibliometric approach included performance analysis (scientific production, author affiliations, most cited journals, and collaboration networks) and thematic analysis (keyword frequency, research trends over time, co-occurrence networks, longitudinal thematic evolution, and thematic maps). The analysis highlights a substantial increase in research output over the studied period and identifies key contributors and geographical patterns in the field. It reveals important gaps in the literature, particularly regarding the relationship between emerging digitalization components (e.g., remote work, Internet of Things (IoT), virtual reality, blockchain) and mental health. In addition, the findings indicate the rapid emergence of new research directions driven by technological advances, especially in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital environments. This study provides a baseline overview of the field prior to the accelerated expansion of AI-driven research observed after mid-2024. The findings have important implications for mental health research prioritization, clinical awareness, and the development of evidence-based interventions addressing the psychological impact of emerging digital technologies.

title: Exploring ESG Dimensions in the Urban Context
summary: This article provides a critical and thematically structured literature review of Envi-ronmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) urbanism as it intersects with the right to the city, green gentrification, affordable housing, public-private partnerships, and partici-patory governance. Drawing from over 100 peer-reviewed sources published between 2020 and 2025, the study examines how ESG frameworks are adopted, contested, and operationalized across diverse urban contexts. While ESG has emerged as a dominant paradigm in urban planning and real estate, the review reveals its frequent co-optation by market-driven agendas, which risk reproducing socio-spatial inequalities under the guise of sustainability. At the same time, the literature highlights promising alternatives rooted in environmental justice, multispecies ethics, legal reform, and community-led planning. The review advances the argument that ESG must be reframed not as a universal compliance model, but as a situated, justice-oriented framework capable of responding to the complex ecological and social realities of contemporary urbanization. By foregrounding relational governance, inclusive design, and equitable urban futures, the article contributes to an emerging research agenda that challenges technocratic sus-tainability and reclaims ESG as a transformative tool for spatial and environmental justice.

summary: هدف البحث إلى تحليل أثر التحول الرقمي في فاعلية الذات لدى الأفراد، وتحديد أبعاده النفسية، والكشف عن الفرص التي تتيحها التقنيات الرقمية لتعزيز الثقة بالقدرة على الإنجاز والتكيف مع المتغيرات المعاصرة. واعتمد البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، من خلال مراجعة الأدبيات النظرية والدراسات السابقة المتعلقة بالتحول الرقمي وفاعلية الذات وتحليلها. وأظهرت النتائج أن التحول الرقمي لا يقتصر على توظيف التقنيات الحديثة، بل يمثل تحولًا شاملًا في أساليب العمل والتعلم وتقديم الخدمات، بما يسهم في تنمية مهارات التعلم الذاتي والوصول إلى المعلومات والتكيف مع البيئات الإلكترونية. كما تبين أن امتلاك المهارات الرقمية يرتبط بتعزيز ثقة الفرد بقدرته على النجاح والإنجاز، وأن ارتفاع فاعلية الذات يساعد على تقليل القلق ومقاومة التغيير عند الانتقال من النظم التقليدية إلى النظم الرقمية. وفي المقابل، يؤدي ضعف البنية التحتية الرقمية، ومحدودية الدعم الفني، وصعوبة الوصول إلى المعلومات إلى انخفاض الشعور بفاعلية الذات. وأكد البحث أهمية الدعم المؤسسي في تخفيف الآثار النفسية المصاحبة للتحول الرقمي وتعزيز قدرة الأفراد على التكيف معه. وأوصى بتطوير البنية التحتية والمنصات التعليمية الرقمية، وتنظيم برامج تدريبية لأعضاء هيئة التدريس والطلبة، وتوفير المختبرات الافتراضية، وتعزيز الأمن السيبراني، ودمج تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي واستراتيجيات التدريس الرقمية في العملية التعليمية.

title: Climate change, ESG–based sustainability uncertainty and insurance expansion
summary: Purpose This paper aims to examine the combined effects of climate risk and environmental, social, and governance (ESG)-related uncertainty on insurance companies across a panel of 11 countries. Design/methodology/approach This study uses the annual time series data related to 11 countries, ranging from 2010 to the 2023. The authors use the panel quantile autoregressive distributed lag regression and Granger non-causality analysis techniques. Findings The findings show significant heterogeneity across quantiles in the determinants of insurance expansion. ESG-related sustainability uncertainty promotes insurance growth in the long run, especially in higher quantiles, while climate performance improves insurance revenues in the short run, mainly in lower quantiles. In contrast, climate change uncertainty has an immediate positive effect in countries with low insurance premiums, but its long-term impact diminishes in high-premium markets. These findings are consistent with stakeholder theory and institutional theory. Practical implications Climate and ESG-related sustainability uncertainty require policy frameworks that account for the unintended effects of mitigation measures on insurers’ risk assessment and pricing while ensuring the affordability of climate-related microinsurance. Integrating uncertainty into risk models and aligning insurance practices with sustainability goals improves risk estimation and enhances the long-term resilience of the insurance sector. Originality/value The authors results contribute to the existing literature on ESG and climate-related uncertainty in insurance market expansion and provide useful insights for policymakers and insurance practitioners.

title: Structure or Composition? Explaining the ESG Premium in Firm Profitability With Oaxaca and Pseudo‐Panel Evidence
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether ESG‐related profitability differences arise from observable firm characteristics or from structural differences in how firms convert those characteristics into performance outcomes. Using an unbalanced panel data design, the final sample comprises 727 firm‐year observations from 178 publicly listed non‐financial firms across 11 MENA countries and 10 economic sectors, covering the fiscal years from 2016 to 2023. The analysis combines fixed‐effects estimation, system GMM, Blinder–Oaxaca decomposition, and a cohort‐based pseudo‐panel framework. The results show that the positive cross‐sectional relationship between ESG and profitability disappears after controlling for firm‐fixed effects, indicating that ESG premiums are primarily driven by persistent firm characteristics rather than within‐firm ESG improvements. Dynamic panel and lagged specifications provide limited evidence of a causal effect of ESG on profitability. Blinder–Oaxaca decomposition results indicate that observable firm characteristics explain only a small share of the profitability gap between high‐ and low‐ESG firms, while most of the gap reflects differences in the estimated returns to those characteristics rather than differences in firm composition. Overall, the findings suggest that ESG‐related profitability differences are predominantly structural rather than compositional.

title: Fintech Impact MSME Financial Performance Mediated by Digitalization and Moderated by Sustainability Practices
summary: Purpose: This study investigates the impact of financial technology (fintech) adoption on the financial performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Specifically, it examines the mediating role of business digitalization and the moderating influence of sustainability practices on this relationship. Method: Employing a quantitative research design, primary data were gathered via structured questionnaires from 155 MSME owners and managers in Yogyakarta who utilize fintech in their business operations. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling via SmartPLS, encompassing measurement model assessment, structural model evaluation, and hypothesis testing. Finding: The results demonstrate that fintech adoption exerts a positive and statistically significant influence on both business digitalization and MSME financial performance. Furthermore, business digitalization is positively and significantly associated with improved financial performance, serving as a partial mediator in the relationship between fintech utilization and financial performance. Additionally, sustainability practices significantly moderate this relationship, specifically attenuating the positive effect of business digitalization on MSME financial performance. Novelty: The novelty of this research lies in the integration of business digitalization as a mediator and sustainability as a moderator within a comprehensive model, providing nuanced insights into the dynamics of fintech adoption and financial performance within the MSME sector in Yogyakarta.

title: Financial Development and Economic Development in Africa: A Systematic Review on the Mediating Role of FinTech
summary: This systematic review examines the mediating role of financial technology (FinTech) in the relationship between financial development and economic development across African economies. It draws on 34 empirical studies published between 2019 and 2026, identified through a structured search of six electronic databases, namely Scopus, ScienceDirect, JSTOR, DOAJ, SciELO, and ERIC. The search was supplemented by manual reference screening. The review synthesises evidence on how digital financial innovations, including mobile money, digital banking, and electronic payment systems, expand financial inclusion and influence economic outcomes. Grounded in Financial Intermediation Theory, Financial Development Theory, Financial Inclusion Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model, the review provides a coherent framework for understanding FinTech as a structural mediator rather than an independent growth driver. Studies were assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT, 2018). The findings indicate that FinTech significantly amplifies the positive effects of financial development on economic growth, poverty reduction, and financial inclusion, though these effects are often nonlinear and context-dependent. Institutional quality, regulatory frameworks, and technological infrastructure emerge as critical moderating conditions. This review contributes to the literature by providing the first systematic synthesis that explicitly classifies included studies by their capacity to formally test mediation versus those that imply indirect mechanisms, offering a more precise account of the FinTech–financial development–economic development nexus in Africa. The findings yield targeted policy recommendations for central banks, financial regulators, commercial banks, telecommunications providers, and government policymakers.

title: VAT in the Digital Economy: Practical Challenges to Implementing the Destination Principle and VAT Collection Mechanisms in Africa
summary: VAT has become the most significant source of tax revenue in many African jurisdictions, rising to an average of 4.5% of gross domestic product in 2022. However, the practical application of the destination principle, which requires taxing final consumption in the jurisdiction of the consumer, and VAT collection mechanisms to support the destination principle, especially on supplies of cross-border services and intangibles, remains technically and administratively challenging. While some countries in Africa have introduced VAT rules on digital services with measurable revenue gains, the adoption of similar rules remains limited across much of the continent. In this article, the authors examine the implementation of internationally agreed standards on cross-border VAT in African countries, highlighting varying approaches adopted by African countries.

title: THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CYBERSECURITY RISK ASSESSMENT AND AUDIT PERFORMANCE
summary: There have been transformations in business processes, accounting practices, and organisational decision making due to the rising use of digital technology. Organisational systems are prone to sophisticated cyber security threats such as ransomware attacks, phishing attacks, malware, insider threats, and unauthorized access to systems despite these technological advancements that have helped boost efficiency. These pose serious threats to the availability, confidentiality, and integrity of organisational information that will affect accounting practices and auditing. By using a comprehensive examination of the literature, auditing standards, and cybersecurity frameworks used around the world, this study aims to examine the relationship between cybersecurity risk assessment and audit performance. Cybersecurity risk assessment improves audit planning, internal control assessment, audit quality, compliance with regulations, and overall audit performance, according to the study that uses descriptive research design and qualitative content analysis on secondary sources. To improve audit performance, the study finds that cybersecurity risk assessment is now an indispensable component of auditing and recommends continuous monitoring of cybersecurity, adoption of advanced technology, and collaboration between auditors and cybersecurity professionals.
